chunks: that a man said to Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him): 'I entrusted a man with wealth that I had deposited with him, but he betrayed me and denied my wealth.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The trustworthy one did not betray you, but you entrusted the betrayer.'

key_terms.ائْتَمَنْتُ: I entrusted / I made a trust
key_terms.الصَّادِقُ: Al-Sadiq (the Truthful), a title for Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the reason for betrayal when entrusting wealth to someone?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the abstract virtue of amanah (trustworthiness) and the specific character of the trustee, teaching that one is not betrayed by the concept of trust but by the inherent nature of the chosen individual. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on discernment (tabyin) in social contracts, where the reliability of the depositary is contingent upon their personal integrity rather than the mere act of entrusting. The narration serves as a practical legal and ethical guideline for verifying the moral standing of those entrusted with wealth or secrets.
